key_insight: LCA is a model-agnostic orchestration layer that separates oncology data routing from AI inference so different black-box models can be swapped without changing the workflow.
clinical_relevance: This could make clinical decision support systems in oncology more modular, resilient to IT changes, and easier to integrate across multimodal patient data streams.
method: Defines LCA as a 7-tuple orchestration architecture with strict separation from underlying AI models
Uses an Entry Theory based on Geometric Deep Learning to normalize multimodal patient data
Routes data through a Cancer Switching Module and emits a Standardized Intermediate Payload (SIP) for downstream processing
evidence_signal: A proof-of-concept tested four technical scenarios, showing negligible orchestration overhead, invariant routing during model swaps, and 100% recall for targeted supplementary data requests under injected anomalies.
watch_item: The framework was validated only in proof-of-concept settings, so real-world clinical integration, interoperability, and workflow safety still need broader testing.
paper_title: The Large Cancer Assistant (LCA): A Model-Agnostic Orchestration Framework for Scalable Clinical Decision Support in Oncology
